fullPassage: People may not think critically for a variety of reasons, such as laziness and inability, but fear is a big one. Why is that? People don't want to think not just because it's hard, but also because they're afraid it will make them question their long-held beliefs. Your students most likely do want to think about things that can be very controversial, like politics, ethics, and philosophy. But probe even deeper. Once we start thinking deeply, long-held assumptions are challenged. Thought makes us worry that we'll lose our balance and have to look at the world in a different way. We worry about thinking because we care about what we and other people think. Even the most far-fetched ideas have an effect on the world. Non-Euclidean geometry and symbolic logic are about as abstract as thinking can get, but you can't understand Einsteinian gravity without the first and run computers without the second. Thinking is important to us, to others, and to the world we live in. This is one reason why we are so afraid of it: it shakes us to the core.

questions.passage: People may not think (A) for a variety of reasons. Your students most likely do want to think about things that can be very (B), like politics, ethics, and philosophy. Once we start thinking deeply, long-held assumptions are (C).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 비판적으로(critically) 생각하고, 논쟁적(controversial)인 것들, 가정이 도전받는다(challenged).
det.analysis:
✅ ① critically — controversial — challenged: 원문과 일치
❌ ② superficially: critically의 반의어
❌ ③ trivial: controversial의 반의어
❌ ④ confirmed: challenged의 반의어
❌ ⑤ 세 단어 모두 불일치

questions.passage: Non-Euclidean geometry and symbolic logic are about as (A) as thinking can get, but you can't understand Einsteinian gravity without the first. Thinking is (B) to us, to others, and to the world. This is one reason why we are so afraid of it: it (C) us to the core.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① abstract — important — shakes: 원문과 일치
❌ ② concrete: abstract의 반의어
❌ ③ trivial: important의 반의어
❌ ④ soothes: shakes의 반의어
❌ ⑤ 세 단어 모두 불일치

questions.passage: People may not think <u>① critically</u> for a variety of reasons. Your students want to think about things that can be very <u>② controversial</u>. Long-held assumptions are <u>③ challenged</u>. Non-Euclidean geometry is about as <u>④ abstract</u> as thinking can get. Thinking is <u>⑤ insignificant</u> to us and to the world.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ⑤ insignificant → important: 사고가 중요하다(important)는 문맥.
det.analysis:
✅ ① critically: 비판적으로, 적절
✅ ② controversial: 논쟁적인, 적절
✅ ③ challenged: 도전받는, 적절
✅ ④ abstract: 추상적인, 적절
❌ ⑤ insignificant(하찮은) → important(중요한): 반의어

questions.passage: People may not think critically because of <u>① laziness</u> and inability. They're <u>② afraid</u> it will make them question their long-held <u>③ beliefs</u>. Thought makes us worry that we'll <u>④ maintain</u> our balance. It shakes us to the <u>⑤ core</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ maintain → lose: 균형을 잃을까(lose) 걱정하지, 유지할까(maintain) 걱정하는 것이 아닙니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① laziness: 게으름, 적절
✅ ② afraid: 두려운, 적절
✅ ③ beliefs: 신념, 적절
❌ ④ maintain(유지하다) → lose(잃다): 반의어
✅ ⑤ core: 핵심, 적절
det.tip: lose our balance(균형을 잃다) ≠ maintain our balance(균형을 유지하다)

questions.passage: Non-Euclidean geometry and symbolic logic are about as <u>abstract</u> as thinking can get.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>abstract</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ theoretical(이론적인): abstract의 동의어
❌ concrete(구체적인): 반의어
❌ practical(실용적인): 반의어
❌ simple(단순한): 다른 의미
❌ obvious(명백한): 다른 의미

questions.passage: Your students want to think about things that can be very <u>controversial</u>, like politics, ethics, and philosophy.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>controversial</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ debatable(논쟁적인): controversial의 동의어
❌ common(흔한): 다른 의미
❌ boring(지루한): 다른 의미
❌ simple(단순한): 다른 의미
❌ accepted(인정된): controversial의 반의어

questions.passage: Even the most <u>far-fetched</u> ideas have an effect on the world.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 far-fetched와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ conventional(전통적인, 상식적인): far-fetched의 반의어
❌ creative(창의적인): 유사하지만 반의어 아님
❌ logical(논리적인): 다른 차원
❌ progressive(진보적인): 다른 차원
❌ traditional(전통적인): conventional과 유사

questions.passage: Once we start thinking deeply, long-held assumptions are <u>challenged</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 challenged와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ confirmed(확인된): challenged의 반의어
❌ questioned: challenged의 유의어
❌ examined: 유사 의미
❌ tested: 유사 의미
❌ investigated: 유사 의미

questions.passage: People may not think critically for a variety of reasons, such as laziness and inability, but __________ is a big one. People don't want to think because they're afraid it will make them question their beliefs.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 비판적 사고를 하지 않는 가장 큰 이유 = 두려움(fear).
det.analysis:
✅ fear(두려움): afraid, worry 등과 연결
❌ laziness: 이미 언급됨
❌ inability: 이미 언급됨
❌ courage: 문맥과 반대
❌ curiosity: 문맥과 반대

questions.passage: Once we start thinking deeply, long-held __________ are challenged. Thought makes us worry that we'll lose our balance.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ assumptions(가정): long-held assumptions = 오래된 가정
❌ experiments: 실험
❌ observations: 관찰
❌ calculations: 계산
❌ predictions: 예측

questions.passage: you can't understand Einsteinian gravity without the first and <u>run</u> computers without the second.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 run이 글에서 의미하는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ 작동시키다: run computers = 컴퓨터를 실행하다
❌ 달리다: run fast의 의미
❌ 경영하다: run a business의 의미
❌ 흐르다: 물이 흐르다
❌ 출마하다: run for office의 의미

questions.passage: But <u>probe</u> even deeper. Once we start thinking deeply, long-held assumptions are challenged.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 probe가 글에서 의미하는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ 탐구하다/파고들다: probe deeper = 더 깊이 파고들다
❌ 찌르다: 물리적 의미
❌ 조사하다: investigate에 가까움
❌ 검사하다: examine에 가까움
❌ 찾아보다: look up에 가까움
det.tip: probe = 탐구하다, 깊이 파고들다 (사고의 깊이를 강조)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a thing that is accepted as true or as certain to happen, without proof"

det.korean: 증거 없이 사실이거나 일어날 것으로 받아들여지는 것 → assumption(가정).
det.analysis:
✅ assumption(가정): 증거 없이 받아들여지는 것
❌ laziness(게으름): 다른 의미
❌ inability(무능): 다른 의미
❌ courage(용기): 다른 의미
❌ curiosity(호기심): 다른 의미
det.tip: assumption = 가정, 전제 (증거 없이 받아들이는 것)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"unlikely and unconvincing; implausible"

det.korean: 있을 법하지 않고 설득력 없는; 믿기 어려운 → far-fetched(터무니없는).
det.analysis:
✅ far-fetched(터무니없는): unlikely + unconvincing
❌ concrete(구체적인): 반대
❌ practical(실용적인): 반대
❌ conventional(전통적인): 반대
❌ logical(논리적인): 반대

questions.passage: People may not think __________ (critical) for a variety of reasons, such as laziness and inability.
questions.stem: 주어진 단어를 문맥에 맞게 어형을 변환하여 빈칸에 쓰시오.

det.analysis:
critical → critically: 형용사 → 부사
동사 수식 → 부사 필요

questions.passage: People may not think critically for a variety of reasons, such as laziness and __________ (able).
questions.stem: 주어진 단어를 문맥에 맞게 어형을 변환하여 빈칸에 쓰시오.

det.analysis:
able → inability: 형용사 → 명사(in- + ability)
laziness and inability = 게으름과 무능

questions.passage: Thinking is important to us, to others, and to the world we live in. This is one reason why we are so afraid of it: it __________.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사고가 우리를 핵심까지 흔든다(shakes us to the core).
det.analysis:
✅ shakes us to the core: 원문과 일치
❌ rewards us: 보상이 아님
❌ calms us: 두려움과 모순
❌ strengthens us: 두려움과 모순
❌ entertains us: 두려움과 모순
det.tip: shakes us to the core = 우리를 근본부터 흔든다

questions.passage: Thought makes us worry that we'll lose our balance and have to __________.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 균형을 잃고 세상을 다른 방식으로 봐야(look at the world in a different way) 할까 걱정한다.
det.analysis:
✅ look at the world in a different way: 원문과 일치
❌ strengthen our beliefs: 반대
❌ reinforce our views: 반대
❌ ignore our surroundings: 무관
❌ accept our limitations: 무관
det.tip: look at the world in a different way = 세상을 다른 시각으로 보다

ch: look at the world in a different way

questions.passage: People may not think critically for a variety of reasons, such as laziness and inability, but __________ is a big one. Why is that? People don't want to think not just because it's hard, but also because they're afraid.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 가장 큰 이유는 두려움(fear). afraid와 직접 연결.
det.analysis:
✅ fear: afraid와 직접 연결

❌ joy: 무관

questions.passage: People don't want to think not just because it's hard, but also because they're afraid it will make them __________ their long-held beliefs.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ question(의문을 제기하다): 신념을 의심하다
❌ strengthen: 강화하다 (두려움과 모순)
❌ simplify: 단순화하다
❌ eliminate: 제거하다
❌ promote: 촉진하다
